cf.title: Add pg_get_table_ddl() to reconstruct CREATE TABLE statements

input.subject: [PATCH] Add pg_get_table_ddl() to reconstruct CREATE TABLE statements

verdict_reasoning: The goal has shown interest from several users, so level 1b does not stop the review. The design does: prior-attempts-1 shows the signature follows sibling functions that were reverted pending a redesign, and the thread has no answer on how this patch follows it. standards-compat-1 shows that v26 changes pg_get_constraintdef() output and breaks pg_dump --no-tablespaces. maintenance-fit-1 adds that no in-tree test keeps this function in sync with pg_dump.

brief.title: Add pg_get_table_ddl() to reconstruct a table's DDL
brief.problem: Postgres has no server-side function that returns the full DDL for a table. The author extends the pg_get_database/role/tablespace_ddl family to tables, for tools and for users who clone schemas, for example in a multi-tenant setup.
brief.proposed_design: A set-returning function returns the CREATE TABLE statement and the follow-up ALTER TABLE, CREATE INDEX, CREATE RULE and CREATE STATISTICS statements, one per row. It calls existing ruleutils.c deparse helpers plus new thin wrappers, and omits any clause whose value equals the default. Named boolean parameters control formatting, and only_kinds or except_kinds arrays filter which object classes it emits.
user_visible_surface: SQL function pg_get_table_ddl(relation regclass, pretty, owner, tablespace, schema_qualified boolean, only_kinds text[], except_kinds text[]) returning setof text
Kind vocabulary: table, index, primary_key, unique, check, foreign_key, exclusion, rule, statistics, trigger, policy, rls, replica_identity, partition
schema_qualified parameter, which narrows search_path to pg_catalog or to the table's own schema during deparse
Changed output of pg_get_constraintdef(): EXCLUDE constraints now include USING INDEX TABLESPACE (reported in message #73)
author_claims: Reusing the ruleutils.c helpers avoids new pg_get_index_ddl or pg_get_constraint_ddl wrappers.
A pg_regress test with exact .out diffs checks a deparse function better than TAP.
Sharing code with pg_dump's dumpTableSchema is impractical; pg_dump could later call this function instead.
A reviewer's round-trip against pg_dump on v25 found 509 of 563 regression tables identical, with the rest by design or deferred.
brief.thread_state: Zsolt Parragi, Rui Zhao, Kyotaro Horiguchi, Chao Li and Marcos Pegoraro reviewed through v26, and Rui reports no open items. Marcos then pointed out that the sibling pg_get_*_ddl commits were reverted pending a redesign, and Henson Choi reported a pg_dump --no-tablespaces regression from the changed pg_get_constraintdef(); the author has answered neither.
unclear: The material does not say how the revert and the "pg_get_*_ddl() needs a redesign" thread affect this patch's interface.
The patch does not say which callers of pg_get_constraintdef_worker() should get the new tablespace clause, or whether that change is intended.
Partition children with a different column order and child constraint names after ATTACH are deferred, and no follow-up design is given.
Triggers, policies, owned sequences, comments, grants and security labels are not emitted, and the material does not say how users get complete DDL.
The material does not say how pg_dump and this function will stay in sync as new table features land.
search_queries: server side create table ddl function

prior_attempts.title: psql: add \si, \sm, \st and \sr functions to show CREATE commands for indexes, matviews, triggers and tables
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P14 put CREATE output for tables and other objects in psql commands. This proposal is a server-side SQL function. P14's reason is not recorded.

prior_attempts.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
prior_attempts.quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.
prior_attempts.reason: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P4 deparsed DDL commands from parse trees for replication. This proposal deparses catalog state for one table, but it is also a hand-written deparser that must follow every DDL change.

prior_attempts.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
prior_attempts.quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.
prior_attempts.reason: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 changed schema qualification in pg_get_constraintdef call by call. This patch narrows search_path during deparse and adds thin ruleutils.c wrappers.

objections.title: Extends a function family that was reverted pending a redesign
objections.failure_scenario: The patch is committed with the named-boolean signature copied from pg_get_role_ddl() and its siblings. The redesign of the reverted siblings then picks a different option model or output contract. Either pg_get_table_ddl() ships out of line with its family, or its interface changes again before or after release.
objections.argument: Message #39 bases the v14+ signature on a commit to pg_get_role_ddl(), pg_get_tablespace_ddl() and pg_get_database_ddl(). Message #72 reports that those commits were reverted, with a thread titled "pg_get_*_ddl() needs a redesign". The thread does not reply to message #72, and the material does not say what the redesign changes. A committer would likely ask that this patch wait for, or follow, that redesign.
objections.author_must_show: Which parts of this interface depend on the reverted sibling design, and how does the patch follow the outcome of the redesign thread?

critic.reasoning: Message #39 ties the signature to the sibling functions, and message #72 reports those commits were reverted pending a redesign. The thread has no reply, so the material offers nothing to refute this with.

objections.title: Changed pg_get_constraintdef() output breaks pg_dump --no-tablespaces
objections.failure_scenario: An admin dumps a database with an EXCLUDE constraint in tablespace xts using `pg_dump --no-tablespaces`, then restores it where xts does not exist. The ADD CONSTRAINT fails with `tablespace "xts" does not exist` and the constraint is lost. psql \d also shows the tablespace twice.
objections.argument: Message #73 shows that the patch changed the shared pg_get_constraintdef_worker(), so every existing caller now sees a different result: pg_dump, pg_restore, psql \d, and ALTER COLUMN TYPE rebuilds. The proposal does not say whether this change is intended outside pg_get_table_ddl(). The thread has no answer to message #73. A committer would likely ask that existing SQL-visible output stay byte-identical unless a separate, justified change is proposed.
objections.author_must_show: Can the tablespace clause be limited to pg_get_table_ddl()'s own wrapper, with pg_get_constraintdef() output unchanged for all existing callers?

critic.reasoning: Message #73 gives a reproduction on v26 and names the affected callers. The author has not answered, and the commit message does not list a change to pg_get_constraintdef() output.

objections.title: Second copy of pg_dump's table logic with no in-tree sync check
objections.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new table property, and the commit updates pg_dump's dumpTableSchema but not ddlutils.c. pg_get_table_ddl() then emits DDL that replays without error but loses the property. Users who clone schemas with it find the difference only when behaviour changes in production.
objections.argument: Messages #4 to #70 show about 25 rounds in which reviewers found silent fidelity gaps by diffing against pg_dump by hand. Rui's round-trip check (messages #51, #55, #64, #70) is the only thing that caught them, and it is not part of the patch. Kyotaro raised the overlap in message #42. The author's answer in message #44 that pg_dump could call this later leaves two implementations in the meantime. [P4] was stopped over the same cost of a hand-written deparser that every DDL change must also update.
objections.author_must_show: Which in-tree test fails when a new table feature is added to pg_dump but not to pg_get_table_ddl()?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Message #44 defers the pg_dump switch, so two generators remain, and the round-trip check that found the gaps is not in the patch. [P4] concerns a parse-tree deparser for replication, but its recorded maintenance reason applies here too.

objections.title: Single all-or-nothing patch mixes helper changes with the new function
objections.failure_scenario: A committer reviewing the 320 KB patch focuses on ddlutils.c and misses a behaviour change in a ruleutils.c or tablecmds.c helper. The change ships and breaks an unrelated caller, as message #73 found for pg_get_constraintdef(). Nobody notices until a user's restore fails.
objections.argument: v26 changes ruleutils.c, tablecmds.c and pg_inherits.c, and adds the new function, all in one commit. The new wrappers (pg_get_indexdef_ddl, pg_get_constraintdef_body and others) and the exported helpers could go first as separate commits, each with tests showing that existing output does not change. That split would have exposed the regression in message #73 by itself. [P3] was returned partly because the qualification rules in ruleutils.c call sites were not defined.
objections.author_must_show: Can the ruleutils.c and tablecmds.c changes be split into a preparatory patch whose tests show no change for existing callers?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: v26 is one patch that touches ruleutils.c, tablecmds.c and pg_inherits.c, and message #73 shows a shared-helper change reached existing callers unnoticed through 26 versions. [P3] is about qualification rules and must not be used as support.

objections.title: Partial output where pg_dump --schema-only -t already gives complete DDL
objections.failure_scenario: A user clones a tenant schema with pg_get_table_ddl() as Marcos describes in message #3. Triggers, policies, grants, comments and the sequences behind serial columns are missing. Inserts fail on the missing sequence or bypass the trigger, and the user notices only in production.
objections.argument: pg_dump --schema-only -t and -n already produce complete, replayable table DDL, including the objects this function leaves out by design (messages #52, #60). What the proposal adds is a call from SQL without a client tool, and the commit message advertises a "full definition" that the function does not deliver. A committer would likely ask whether SQL-level access to a subset of pg_dump's output is worth a permanent second implementation, given that users who need complete DDL still need pg_dump.
objections.author_must_show: Which users cannot run pg_dump --schema-only -t, and is the subset this function emits enough for them without pg_dump?

critic.reasoning: Messages #3, #15 and #35 show interest from independent users, which lowers the weight of this objection. But the thread never says why pg_dump --schema-only -t does not serve them, and the function omits objects pg_dump emits.

other_surviving.title: Reserved trigger and policy kinds change default output later
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user writes a schema-clone script that uses the default output. After a later major upgrade, triggers and policies start to appear in that output, and the script fails because the trigger functions do not exist on the target. A user who passes only_kinds => ARRAY['trigger'] today gets zero rows and no error.
other_surviving.argument: The commit message says trigger and policy "are accepted in the vocabulary but currently produce no output" and are reserved for future helpers. So the default output, which has no filter, is defined as incomplete today, and its meaning will grow in a later release. Accepting a kind that does nothing also hides user mistakes, while unknown kinds raise an error. A committer would likely ask for an error, or for these kinds to stay out of the vocabulary until they work.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why accept trigger and policy now as no-ops instead of rejecting them, and how will the default output stay stable for existing callers once they are implemented?

critic.reasoning: The commit message confirms that trigger and policy are accepted and emit nothing, while unknown kinds raise an error. The point about default output growing later is weaker, since any deparse function grows with new features, but the silent no-op stands.

other_surviving.title: schema_qualified adds a qualification rule unlike other deparse functions
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A tool replays schema_qualified => false output under a new search_path to clone a schema. A referenced object outside the table's schema comes out unqualified or qualified depending on helper visibility rules, so the clone binds to the wrong object, or touches the source schema as in message #68.
other_surviving.argument: Message #35 notes that no other pg_get_*def or pg_get_*ddl function has such an option, and that callers already control qualification through search_path. Message #36 keeps the option "for per-call convenience" and implements it by narrowing search_path. Review found qualification bugs in messages #38, #41 and #68. [P3] stalled on a similar point: a committer asked for a defined rule on which ruleutils call sites qualify names.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What documented rule decides which names each ruleutils wrapper qualifies, and what does schema_qualified do that setting search_path before the call does not?

precedents.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled

critic.reasoning: Message #36 keeps the option only "for per-call convenience" and does not say what it does that setting search_path cannot. The bugs in the scenario were fixed by v25 (message #70), and [P3] gives only loose support.

refuted.title: Second hand-written table deparser with nothing to keep it in sync
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a table clause or column property and teaches pg_dump's dumpTableSchema about it. No test fails for pg_get_table_ddl(). Users who clone schemas with it lose that property without any error, and they notice only when behavior differs on the copy.
refuted.argument: [P4] stalled because a hand-written DDL deparser must change whenever DDL changes, and that reason applies here. Message #42 raised the overlap with dumpTableSchema. Message #44 answers that pg_dump could call the function later, but nothing in the patch makes that happen. The thread needed 26 versions and repeated pg_dump round-trip sweeps (messages #51, #55, #64, #70) to find gaps, and that check is not part of the patch.
refuted.author_must_show: What fails in the build or tests when a new table feature reaches pg_dump but not pg_get_table_ddl()?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1, which states the same point and names the missing in-tree check more directly.

refuted.title: Signature follows a sibling family that was reverted for redesign
refuted.failure_scenario: pg_get_table_ddl() ships with named boolean parameters copied from pg_get_role/tablespace/database_ddl(). The redesign of that family then settles on a different interface. Users end up with one DDL function that behaves unlike its siblings, or face a signature change after release.
refuted.argument: The commit message bases the signature on "the named-parameter convention established by pg_get_role_ddl(), pg_get_tablespace_ddl(), and pg_get_database_ddl()". Message #72 reports that those commits were reverted pending a redesign, and the thread has no reply on how this patch fits it. A user-facing function contract is hard to change after release, so a committer would likely want the family's interface settled first.
refuted.author_must_show: How does this interface fit the outcome of the pg_get_*_ddl() redesign discussion, and which parameters would change if that discussion picks another shape?

refuted.title: Shared pg_get_constraintdef() change alters pg_dump output and index placement
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA runs `pg_dump --no-tablespaces` against a patched server that has an EXCLUDE constraint in tablespace xts, then restores on a host without xts. The ADD CONSTRAINT fails and the constraint is lost, and the DBA finds out only at restore time. Separately, `alter table ... alter column ... type bigint` now rebuilds the index in xts instead of the default tablespace.
refuted.argument: Message #73 shows that adding USING INDEX TABLESPACE in pg_get_constraintdef_worker() changes output for every caller: pg_dump, pg_restore --no-tablespaces, psql \d, and the ALTER COLUMN TYPE rebuild path. pg_dump passes the tablespace only through SET default_tablespace, so the new clause bypasses --no-tablespaces and ends up in archives on disk. The author has not answered message #73, and the commit message does not list this as an intended change to an existing function.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the tablespace clause be confined to the pg_get_table_ddl() path so that pg_get_constraintdef(), pg_dump archives and ALTER COLUMN TYPE rebuilds keep their current output and placement?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. Both rest on message #73 and ask for the same confinement of the tablespace clause.

refuted.title: Shared ruleutils change breaks pg_dump --no-tablespaces for EXCLUDE
refuted.failure_scenario: An administrator dumps a database with pg_dump --no-tablespaces and restores it where the tablespace does not exist. Under v26 the EXCLUDE constraint's ADD CONSTRAINT fails, so the constraint is lost. psql \d also shows the tablespace twice, and ALTER COLUMN TYPE keeps the rebuilt index in the old tablespace.
refuted.argument: Message #73 traces the cause to pg_get_constraintdef_worker(), which pg_dump, pg_restore, psql and ALTER TABLE share with the new function. People who never call pg_get_table_ddl() pay for this. The author has not answered message #73. The material does not say which callers should get the new clause.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the ruleutils wrappers be changed so that the output of pg_get_constraintdef() and every existing caller stays the same?

refuted.title: Interface built on a function family that was reverted for redesign
refuted.failure_scenario: The patch is committed with the named boolean parameters and kind vocabulary taken from its siblings. The pg_get_*_ddl redesign then settles on a different interface. The project must either break this function's callers or keep one member of the family on the old interface.
refuted.argument: Message #39 says the signature copies the convention of pg_get_role/tablespace/database_ddl. Message #72 reports that those commits were reverted pending a redesign. The author has not said how the redesign changes this patch. A 320 KB SQL-callable function is hard to change after release, because tools such as schema cloners depend on its output shape.
refuted.author_must_show: What does the pg_get_*_ddl redesign decide about signature and option handling, and does v26 follow that decision?

refuted.title: Second table-DDL generator alongside pg_dump's dumpTableSchema
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new per-column or per-table clause and teaches pg_dump to emit it, but nobody touches ddlutils.c. pg_get_table_ddl() keeps returning DDL that replays cleanly yet drops the new property. Users find out only when a cloned table behaves differently from its source.
refuted.argument: pg_dump already reconstructs table DDL, and Kyotaro objected to the overlap in message #42. The author answered in message #44 that sharing code is impractical and that pg_dump could call this function later, but no such step is proposed, so both generators would be maintained in parallel. Rui's pg_dump comparisons in messages #51 to #70 found dozens of divergences across many rounds, and nothing in the tree would catch a new one. The recorded objection in [P4] was the same: every change to the DDL a hand-written deparser covers also requires a change in that deparser.
refuted.author_must_show: Which in-tree test fails when pg_dump learns a new table clause that pg_get_table_ddl() does not emit, or will pg_dump be switched to call this function?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

refuted.title: Use case not separated from what pg_dump --schema-only -t already gives
refuted.failure_scenario: A user cloning a tenant schema runs pg_get_table_ddl() and replays the output. Triggers, policies, owned sequences, grants, comments and security labels are missing, so serial columns fail on replay. The user then falls back to pg_dump --schema-only -t, which already emits all of these.
refuted.argument: The demand shown is one production interest (message #35), one schema-cloning workflow (messages #3 and #15) and a pgAdmin author. None of these says why a server-side function is needed where pg_dump -t or -n works from the client. Message #44 calls pg_dump calling this function the long-term path but leaves it out of scope, so the function has no in-tree user. Many clauses are omitted on purpose (message #52), so the output is less complete than the workaround it would replace.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users cannot run pg_dump --schema-only -t for their use case, and which tools or workflows would call this function instead?

refuted.title: Every future table feature must also update a second deparser
refuted.failure_scenario: A later release adds a new per-column or per-table option and updates pg_dump but not ddlutils.c. pg_get_table_ddl() then silently omits the clause. A user who replays its output gets a different table and finds out only when behaviour differs.
refuted.argument: The patch is a hand-written reconstruction parallel to dumpTableSchema, and message #42 points out the overlap. About 25 review rounds found gaps by diffing against pg_dump (messages #51 to #70), so the function stays correct only while someone keeps re-running that comparison. The cost lands on every future author of table DDL, while the benefit goes to the few users of this function. [P4] records the same objection to a hand-written DDL deparser.
refuted.author_must_show: What mechanism, such as a test that diffs against pg_dump, fails when a new table feature is added to pg_dump but not to this function?

precedents.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-1. The who-pays framing adds no separate failure scenario.

Can the USING INDEX TABLESPACE clause be limited to pg_get_table_ddl()'s own wrapper, so that pg_get_constraintdef() output stays unchanged for pg_dump, psql and ALTER TABLE?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows ruleutils.c and pg_dump, and who follows the pg_get_*_ddl() redesign thread. No committer speaks in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent SQL-callable interface, for changed ruleutils.c helpers shared with pg_dump and psql, and for keeping a second table DDL generator correct in every later release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted 26 versions through message #71 in response to review. Messages #72 and #73 have no reply yet.

priority.reason: Tool authors and users who clone schemas asked for this in the thread, but the interface follows a function family that was reverted for redesign. The patch is about 320 KiB in one commit and changes ruleutils.c and tablecmds.c helpers that existing callers share.

provisional_note: Only 3 of 73 messages and no code were read, and the content of the redesign thread is not in the material. The permission check, the search_path reset on error and the full set of changed ruleutils.c helpers could not be checked.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix NULL dereference in pg_get_database_ddl()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a NULL check in pg_get_database_ddl_internal() so that a dattablespace pointing to a missing tablespace no longer crashes the backend in pg_strcasecmp(). In that case the function omits the TABLESPACE clause, and a regression test covers it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only reproducer was a manual update of pg_database with allow_system_table_mods, and David Rowley asked why this self-inflicted catalog corruption should matter more than other such cases. The author then found no supported path to the state, because the catalog snapshot keeps both lookups consistent and DROP TABLESPACE fails while the database directory exists, so he withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Can you explain why this method of self-inflicted catalogue corruption
is any more important than any of the just-about-infinite other ways
there are of causing issues by manually updating the catalogue tables?

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Fix pg_get_constraintdef for NOT NULL constraints on domains
Reverted commit(s): Revert structural changes to not-null constraints
precedents_retrieved.objection:
We added pg_constraint rows for all not-null constraints, first for
tables and later for domains; but while the ones for tables were
reverted, the ones for domains were not.  However, we did accidentally
revert ruleutils.c support for the ones on domains in 6f8bb7c1e961,
which breaks running pg_get_constraintdef() on them.  Put that back.

This is only needed in branch 17, because we've reinstated this code in
branch master with commit 14e87ffa5c54.  Add some new tests in both
branches.

I couldn't find anything else that needs de-reverting.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_get_constraintdef: Schema qualify foreign tables unless pretty printing is enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_get_constraintdef schema-qualify the referenced table in a foreign key's REFERENCES clause when pretty printing is off, as pg_get_indexdef already does. The goal is constraint definitions that can be recreated on another system with a different search_path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said pg_get_indexdef is the odd one out, since most generate_relation_name calls in ruleutils.c ignore the pretty flag, and Alvaro Herrera judged the patch too small for making PRETTYFLAG_SCHEMA work consistently. Tom asked for a clearly defined rule on which call sites qualify names, with a documented helper function. The author did not reply to these reviews, and Michael Paquier returned the patch after six weeks without a reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: In other words, I think your patch is too small.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support logical replication of DDL commands
precedents_retrieved.authors: Zheng Li (zhengli), Zhijie Hou (houzj), Ajin Cherian (ajinc), vigneshwaran C (vignesh.postgres), Runqi Tian (runqitian)
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replicate DDL commands through logical replication so that schema changes reach subscribers, for example during major version upgrades. The later patch set deparses DDL commands in event triggers into a JSON format string, WAL-logs it, and the apply worker rebuilds and runs the command, starting with create, alter and drop table.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier objected that the hand-written deparser, with its one-to-one mapping of node enums to hardcoded text, makes every change to the parse node structures of replicated DDL also require a change here. He asked for generated code instead, and the authors argued that much of the deparsing cannot be generated. Work stopped after July 2023, and in March 2024 Amit Kapila said the entry should be closed because it still needs a lot of work.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As presented, this stuff has an extremely high maintenance cost long-term because it requires anybody doing a change in the parsed tree structures of the DDLs replicated to also change the code paths introduced by this patch set.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add callback table access method to reset filenode when dropping relation
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a relation_reset_filenode callback to the table access method interface, called from heap_drop_with_catalog when a table is dropped, as the counterpart of relation_set_new_filenode. The goal was to let table AMs with non-file storage, such as an in-memory table, clean up their storage on DROP TABLE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Heikki Linnakangas pointed out that dropping storage must happen at commit or abort and be redone from the commit record during WAL replay, which cannot run AM-specific code. A callback at drop time, or xact callbacks run at commit, therefore cannot drop storage correctly. Heikki suggested using smgrGetPendingDeletes() instead. The patch then stopped applying, the author did not reply when asked whether he was waiting for feedback, and the entry was marked Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't think implementing dropping relation data at-commit/rollback using
xact callbacks can be correct. The dropping needs to be integrated with the
commit / abort records, so it is redone during crash recovery - that's not
possible with xact callbacks.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump -C Grant statement on create database
precedents_retrieved.summary: When pg_dump is run with -C (emit CREATE DATABASE), it would also emit the database-level GRANT statements (such as GRANT CREATE ON DATABASE), matching what pg_dumpall already produces. The patch makes emitting these grants subject to the existing -x (no privileges) option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The thread contains only the original report, a reply agreeing it is an oversight, and the patch submission; no review or objection to the patch appears, and the entry was returned with feedback about three months later.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return historic snapshot during LR
Reverted commit(s): Don't allow GetTransactionSnapshot() in logical decoding
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1585ff7387 changed GetTransactionSnapshot() to throw an error
if it's called during logical decoding, instead of returning the
historic snapshot. I made that change for extra protection, because a
historic snapshot can only be used to access catalog tables while
GetTransactionSnapshot() is usually called when you're executing
arbitrary queries. You might get very subtle visibility problems if
you tried to use the historic snapshot for arbitrary queries.

There's no built-in code in PostgreSQL that calls
GetTransactionSnapshot() during logical decoding, but it turns out
that the pglogical extension does just that, to evaluate row filter
expressions. You would get weird results if the row filter runs
arbitrary queries, but it is sane as long as you don't access any
non-catalog tables. Even though there are no checks to enforce that in
pglogical, a typical row filter expression does not access any tables
and works fine. Accessing tables marked with the user_catalog_table =
true option is also OK.

To fix pglogical with row filters, and any other extensions that might
do similar things, revert GetTransactionSnapshot() to return a
historic snapshot during logical decoding.

To try to still catch the unsafe usage of historic snapshots, add
checks in heap_beginscan() and index_beginscan() to complain if you
try to use a historic snapshot to scan a non-catalog table. We're very
close to the version 18 release however, so add those new checks only
in master.

precedents_retrieved.title: Ignore attributes of tables part of extensions in pg_dump
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change pg_dump so that getTableAttrs skips fetching column and type information for tables that are members of an extension, using the ext_member flag. The goal was to avoid gathering attributes for tables that pg_dump does not dump individually.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. A reviewer asked why it checked ext_member rather than the usual dobj.dump flag. The author concluded that skipping attributes based on either flag would break binary upgrade, which still dumps extension member tables individually.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Hm. I have been pondering about this code more and I am dropping the patch as either adding a check based on the flag to track dumpable objects or ext_member visibly breaks the logic that binary upgrade and tables in extensions rely on.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_dump new feature: exporting functions only
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a pg_dump switch (--functions-only) to dump only stored functions and procedures from a database, without resolving their dependencies on other objects. During the discussion the design moved toward pattern-based include/exclude options per object type (e.g. --routine/--exclude-routine alongside --table, --schema, --extension).
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for a different design: pattern-matching options per object type with matching exclude options, in line with --table and --extension, instead of an all-or-nothing --functions-only switch. The author summarised the new plan and said she would rewrite the patch, but no reworked patch is shown before the deadline. The committer closing the entry concluded that a different design was wanted and that it would not make v15.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Looks clear to me that a different design is wanted here, and that
this won't make it for v15, so I have marked the patch as returned
with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use JOIN USING aliases in ruleutils.c
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes ruleutils.c so that, when JOIN USING output columns conflict with other names in a query, it attaches generated JOIN USING aliases (a feature added in Postgres 14) and qualifies the columns with them. This replaces the old approach of renaming those columns to be unique across the whole query.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the new output would reduce pg_dump portability, since dumped views would no longer load into pre-v14 servers or other database systems. He also saw little gain: the patch added code to ruleutils.c on net, and the regression test output was not clearly better. The author agreed and withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
My big fear is that it will reduce portability of pg_dump output:
views that would have loaded successfully into pre-v14 servers
no longer will, and your chances of porting them to other RDBMSes
probably go down too.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent in the list rejects a server-side table DDL function. The schema-qualification concern from P3 was settled in the thread.
Apart from the pg_get_constraintdef() side effect, the proposal is a read-only SQL function. It adds a pg_proc entry and no on-disk format, WAL, replication or wire protocol state.

No security objection found. Everything the function emits (columns, defaults, reloptions, constraints, indexes, rules, statistics) is readable today through world-readable catalogs and the existing pg_get_*def functions, and the proposal does not emit policies, grants or security labels. Partition-tree recursion has check_stack_depth (message #65), and the default schema_qualified => true is the safe setting. Not checkable without code: which aclcheck the function applies (message #70 mentions aclcheck_error) and whether narrowing search_path during deparse is undone on error.
Two objections from this angle: the mechanism duplicates pg_dump, and pg_dump already covers the need more completely.

Some demand exists: a production interest in message #35, a multi-tenant cloning workflow in messages #3 and #15, and existing sibling pg_get_*_ddl functions. So the objections ask for more evidence and do not claim the user group is empty.
